_readme: Room/area archetypes. Sizes are INTERIOR clear sizes in blocks: w = x extent, d = z extent, h = floor-to-ceiling clear height (y). Shell adds 1 block each side.
Pick odd w/d so the room has a center line (door and focal point align on it). Ranges = [min, comfortable_max].
Doors: 1 wide x 2 tall is the minimum; main connecting openings should be 3 wide x 3-4 tall. Corridor-to-room openings are centered unless stated.
Coordinates in rules: floor layer y=0, interior y=1..h, ceiling layer y=h+1. Wall faces named N(-z) S(+z) W(-x) E(+x).
Every room needs: one focal point, one light plan that hides its sources, one floor pattern (border or inlay), and at least 3 wall-depth devices (see principles.md D-rules).

archetypes.name: Entrance Hall / Foyer
archetypes.purpose: First impression. Orients the visitor, announces the theme, leads the eye along a main axis.
layout_rules: Single strong axis from the door to the focal point on the far wall; everything symmetric around it.
Doorway 3 wide x 4 tall with an arch or lintel frame (trim) and a 1-block deeper reveal; step up 1 onto the floor (stair/slab).
Floor: bordered rug or inlay on the axis (carpet runner or contrasting strip 3 wide), 1-block border band along walls.
Ceiling higher than neighbouring rooms by 2+; beams or coffers every 3-4 blocks.
Place pillars or half-columns in pairs flanking the axis (2 or 4), at 1/4 and 3/4 depth.
required_features: A focal point on the far wall (feature wall, machine glimpse, banner, statue or big window)
A visible hint of the main machine room through glass or an arch
Light ring or chandelier centered on the axis
Side alcoves or benches so the room is not an empty box

connects.how: Outside door on one short wall; main arch to the showcase hall opposite; side doors 1-wide to corridors at the midpoints of the long walls.

avoid: Empty center with only lights in the ceiling
Ceiling the same height as a corridor

archetypes.name: Storage Room
archetypes.purpose: Chests, barrels, AE2 drives or sorted item storage. Must look ordered and be reachable.
layout_rules: Aisles 3 wide (1 for player, 2 for access) between shelf rows that are 2 deep x 2-3 high.
Shelf rows perpendicular to the entry axis; leave a 3-wide cross aisle in the center.
End walls get feature shelving (barrels, drives) to close the aisle view.
Ceiling beams every 3 blocks over aisles; a lantern/light at every second beam crossing.
Floor: contrasting strip down each aisle center (carpet, different planks).
required_features: Labels: item frame or sign above each shelf bay
A staging table or crafting corner near the door
Ladders or step stools if shelving is 3+ high
At least one decorative cluster (barrel stack, sack pile) breaking the grid

connects.how: Door at one end of the main aisle (3 wide opening), second exit at the far end; do not exit mid-row.

avoid: Chests flat against a bare wall in a line
Uniform ceiling lights directly above every chest

archetypes.name: Crafting / Processing Line
archetypes.purpose: A row of machines (assemblers, presses, inscribers, Create mixers) that visibly flows left to right.
layout_rules: Linear flow along x: input end on W, output on E; show it with a floor lane (3 wide) of a contrasting block and arrow-like chevrons or lights.
Machines in bays of 3 wide x 3 deep with 1-block pillars between; every bay has identical frame, different machine inside.
Pipes/cables run overhead on one side only (cable tray 1 block below ceiling), never across the walking lane.
Raise the machine bays 1 block (slab step) above the walking lane.
Break the monotony every 3rd bay with a taller or wider bay (junction/buffer).
required_features: Walking lane 3 wide down the full length
Per-bay light above machine + one lane light every 4 blocks
Input and output end markers (hopper/chest cluster at start, vault or drive at end)
Glass viewing windows in at least one long wall

connects.how: Both short ends open into rooms (3x4 openings); long walls may have windows to a parallel corridor.

avoid: Machines directly against the wall with no frame

archetypes.name: Server Room (racks)
archetypes.purpose: Rows of drives/interfaces/pattern providers as racks, with hot/cold aisle feel.
layout_rules: Racks in rows: each rack 2 wide x 1 deep x 3 high; rows face a shared 3-wide aisle; leave 1 gap block between rack pairs for cables.
Aisle floor: dark with a light strip (cold aisle) down the center; raised-floor vents (copper_grate) every 4th tile.
Ceiling tray 1 block below ceiling over every aisle; chains down to the racks.
End wall as a status wall: glass + lamps in a grid.
Rack row count odd (3 or 5) so there is a center aisle.
required_features: Per-rack indicator lights (lamps/glass panes on top or front)
Floor light strip hidden under glass
A control desk or terminal nook at the entry

connects.how: Entry through a short airlock-style vestibule (2x3 with doors both ends) on one short wall; second service door opposite.

avoid: Racks flush wall-to-wall with no aisle
Same rack height everywhere (vary with a taller cabinet every 4th)
Bright white everywhere (needs darkness for glow to read)

archetypes.name: Multiblock Showcase Hall
archetypes.purpose: Display a large machine (7x7x7 controller/quantum cube/assembler matrix) as a trophy.
layout_rules: Machine centered on a pedestal/dais; clear space = at least 3 blocks on every side, 4+ on the viewing side, and 2 above (ceiling >= machine height + 4).
Room width/depth = machine size + 2*(3..6) + walls; for a 7-wide machine use 15-19 interior.
Dais: 1-2 steps (stairs) in a square or octagon, 1 larger than the machine on every side, with a contrasting border and a ring of inlay.
Approach axis from the entrance, view from 8-12 blocks away; place a gallery or balcony above for a second view.
Four or eight pillars or buttresses around, framing the machine, taller than it, not hiding it.
required_features: Focus lighting: 4 hidden up-lights on the dais edge or spot lanterns above; avoid lights touching the machine face
Cable/conduit routes in a floor trench or overhead tray, symmetric, ending at the machine ports
Windows or a glass wall so the machine can be seen from the entrance and corridors
Plaque, banner or sign at the dais

connects.how: Grand 5 wide x 5 tall arch from the entrance on the axis; service doors 1-wide at the back; gallery stair at one side.

avoid: Lights directly adjacent to machine blocks (hides texture)

archetypes.name: Corridor / Hallway
archetypes.purpose: Connect rooms, build rhythm, give pacing (compress-then-release).
layout_rules: Width 3 minimum (1 blocking pillar leaves 2 usable), 5 for main routes; ceiling 4-5.
Rhythm: repeat a pattern every 4 blocks (pillar, lamp, window); end with a larger opening or a turn, not a blank wall.
Center strip in the floor in a contrasting block; lights recessed in the ceiling strip, not on the floor.
Doors off the corridor: recessed 1 block with a lintel so the wall has depth.
Add a kink or step down/up every 12-16 blocks to avoid a tube look.
required_features: At least one window or opening to something interesting (room, machine, outdoors)

connects.how: Join rooms at their side centers; T-junctions get a small widened hall (5x5) with a dome/lantern.

archetypes.name: Stairwell
archetypes.purpose: Vertical connection between floors, doubles as a feature.
layout_rules: Stairs 3 wide (2 for tight); each flight 4-6 steps with a landing 3x3 after.
Prefer spiral or switchback; landing every ~3 blocks of rise.
Open a window or glass strip on every landing; place a chandelier hanging in the well.
Handrail: fence/walls/iron_bars on the open side; newel post (log or pillar) at turns.
Headroom: min 3 blocks above every step; use ceiling slabs to keep height.
required_features: Trim line following the stair run (stripe of other block on stringer)

connects.how: Enter on the bottom landing side; exit onto each floor at corridor level with a 3-wide opening.

avoid: No landings on a 10+ block rise

archetypes.name: Atrium
archetypes.purpose: Tall central space tying floors and rooms together; light and view source.
layout_rules: Open from floor to roof; galleries on 2-4 sides at every floor, 3 wide with railings.
Roof: skylight (glass/pane lattice) or dome with ribs every 3 blocks; light wells.
Center feature: tree, fountain, hanging chandelier, or machine.
Colonnade on the ground floor at 4-block spacing, taller than normal columns.
Floor: radial or concentric pattern around the centre.

connects.how: Ground-floor arches 3x4 on all four sides; upper gallery doors every 8-10 blocks.

avoid: Light only from above (no wall sconces)

archetypes.name: Balcony / Gallery / Mezzanine
archetypes.purpose: Elevated viewing platform onto a machine, hall or garden.
layout_rules: Floor 3 wide minimum; rail height 1 block (fence/wall/iron_bars) plus a cap slab if desired.
Corbels (stairs upside down) under the edge or posts below; overhang 1 block gives a shadow line.
Rail posts every 3-4 blocks (taller pillar) with infill; leave a 2-wide gap at the stair/door.
Match the room's trim blocks on the edge fascia.
Place benches or lanterns on posts to use it as a stop-and-look spot.
required_features: Unobstructed view line to the focal point

connects.how: Access via a stair or door at one end; ends at a window or corner bay, not a dead wall.

avoid: Floating slab with no support look

archetypes.name: Garden / Courtyard
archetypes.purpose: Open area outside or in a courtyard; softens hard architecture.
layout_rules: Paths 2-3 wide curving in a loose S or looping; border with slabs/stairs and a contrasting block.
Plant in clusters of odd numbers (3, 5, 7) with 3 height layers: ground cover, mid plants, trees/shrubs.
Terrain gently stepped, mix of grass, moss, coarse dirt, path blocks, gravel.
A water or lighting feature at path junctions (pond, fountain, lantern post).
Boundary: hedges (leaves), walls or fences with gaps, not a hard rectangle.
required_features: At least one focal tree or feature
Lights spaced every 6-8 blocks along paths

connects.how: Gate or arch (3 wide) on the building; the path starts at the door and aims at the focal feature.

archetypes.name: Control Room / Terminal Nook
archetypes.purpose: Where the operator stands: terminals, monitors, overview of a machine.
layout_rules: Raised 1-3 blocks above the machine floor, with a large window wall facing the machine.
Curved or angled desk (slab and stair) in front of the window, 1 block gap behind it for the operator.
Screens (glass panes + lamps) in a bank above desk height; dimmer lighting than the machine room.
Chair/stool positions marked (stairs or carpets).
Cable run visible under glass floor strip.
required_features: Soft ceiling light with a glow strip

connects.how: Back door to a corridor; window faces the hall; side stair to the hall floor.

archetypes.name: Vault / Secure Annex
archetypes.purpose: Small, dramatic, heavy-walled room for high-value storage or the controller core.
layout_rules: Thick walls shown by deep door reveal (3 deep) and a heavy door frame (iron).
Low entrance corridor then a taller chamber: compress then release.
Spotlit central pedestal; dark surrounds; lights from the floor edge and a ceiling oculus.
Lining: alternating dark panels with 1-block metal strips each 3 blocks.
Safe-deposit style shelves in recesses on 2-3 walls.

connects.how: Single door through a 3-deep corridor segment; no windows.

avoid: Thin 1-block walls and a normal door

archetypes.name: Airlock / Vestibule
archetypes.purpose: Small transition cell between contrasting zones (clean/dirty, hot/cold, public/secure).
layout_rules: Door at each end, offset or at least 3 blocks apart; walls in a different material from both sides.
Hazard stripe or contrasting floor, lamp above each door, small window if useful.
Place a bench/rack/console on one side wall.

connects.how: Inline between two rooms; doors on the same axis.

avoid: Door directly opening into the next door

archetypes.name: Machine Bays (alcove row)
archetypes.purpose: A wall of repeated 3-wide alcoves each holding one machine; used for AE2 assemblers, Create units, interfaces.
layout_rules: Alcove 3 wide x 3 high x 2 deep, pillar 1 wide between; machine in the back, lamp above, trim arch on the front.
Every 3rd bay differs (taller, glass front, different accent) to break monotony.
Floor in front: lane strip. Back wall: 1 block recess so shadows read.
required_features: Header beam running the full row

connects.how: Built as the long wall of another room, not a standalone room.

avoid: Same bay pattern repeated 8+ times unbroken

archetypes.name: Reactor / Power Chamber
archetypes.purpose: Huge round/square chamber with a central energy structure and catwalks.
layout_rules: Central core 5-9 wide; 3-5 blocks clearance ring; outer wall 8-12 blocks from the core centre.
Catwalks at 2-3 heights, 3 wide, connected by stairs/ladders; rails everywhere open.
Floor: radial pattern with hazard ring and glow lines to the core.
Ceiling: truss or dome with oculus above the core.
Piping bundles hugging the walls; lighting from the core itself and rim lamps.

connects.how: Two or four large doors on cardinal axes at ground level; control room windows at mid height.

adjacency_hints.pacing: Alternate tall/short and wide/narrow: corridor (3x4) -> hall (15x9) -> corridor -> small vault. Compression makes the next room feel larger.
adjacency_hints.transitions: Between two themes use an airlock_vestibule or a 3-deep door reveal; change floor material at the threshold.
